graft.title: Renaming a node (the root) breaks every rests_on pinned under it: reported as "is gone"
graft.need: After renaming the root node of project dotfiles to vg-dotfiles (proposal 01a146e0-139c, accepted 2026-10-16), tend_basis reports every journal decision and both scores under it as stale with "rests on design:dotfiles / NixOS / Hyprland is gone" (and the like), although the nodes still exist (same ids) under their new path. A rename or move doesn't change what a node is, so pins taken on design:<path> should follow the node (resolve the path to its id when pinned, or re-resolve through the rename), and only a real change to the node's content should make what rests on it stale. Today the only remedy is to restate each decision word for word, superseding it (proposal 01a14718-841d here), which is noise in the journal.
graft.use_case: vg-dotfiles was renamed to match its sibling vg-dotfiles-windows; six decisions and two scores went stale for no reason and had to be re-recorded. Projects will rename and regroup nodes as they grow (design_propose's own docs say regrouping is expected), and each time every decision under the moved part would go falsely stale.

answer.text: In tend 66c2da0 (deployed): a pinned design:<path> that no longer resolves is followed through every path the node has had (its rename, a move, a parent's rename) to where it is now, and compared under its old name: a rename or move alone leaves what rests on it fresh; what the node says changing still makes it stale. The decisions superseded only to re-pin them (proposal 01a14718-841d) aren't needed for that any more.
